The 3D Model With Text block displays an interactive 3D model alongside descriptive content (heading, text, and button). Ideal for showcasing products with rich visual context.
The Blog Posts block displays a grid of blog article cards from a selected blog. It is commonly used in homepage sections, landing pages, or custom layouts to feature recent content.
The Carousel block is a responsive slideshow component based on Bootstrap’s carousel functionality. It supports images, videos, and 3D models as slide content.

The Columns Layout block enables flexible multi-column arrangements within any standard section. It acts as a container for one or more Column blocks, each of which can hold any other block type (e.g., images, text, product cards, forms), allowing for highly customizable side-by-side content layouts.

The Contact Form block is a flexible form component that can be added to any section or layout to collect user input. It supports multiple field types and is suitable for general inquiries, product customization requests, and more.
The Contact Us block is a ready-to-use section that combines a heading, descriptive text, and a contact form—ideal for dedicated contact pages or footer call-to-action areas.

The Countdown Timer block creates a high-impact promotional section that combines rich media with urgency-driven content—ideal for flash sales, product launches, or limited-time offers. It features a two-column layout: one for visual media and one for text-based calls to action.

The Custom Liquid Block allows you to embed raw Liquid code directly into any section of your store. This is useful for advanced customizations, dynamic content, or integrating third-party snippets that require server-side rendering.

The Faq Collapsible Tabs block displays a set of frequently asked questions with collapsible answers. It supports an optional index sidebar for easy navigation and includes a built-in search bar for large FAQ sets.

The Featured Collection block displays products from a selected collection or custom product list using a Swiper-powered carousel with advanced transition effects. Ideal for highlighting seasonal collections, bestsellers, or new arrivals.
The Featured Product block displays a single product with full detail—including media gallery, title, price, variant picker, and buy buttons—allowing customers to purchase directly from any page.

The Hotspots block displays an interactive image with multiple clickable or hoverable points that reveal product or informational cards. Ideal for showcasing featured items within a lifestyle scene, room layout, or product bundle.

The Image With Text block combines a media image with descriptive content (heading, text, and button) in a flexible layout. Ideal for feature highlights, promotional banners, or storytelling sections.

The Key Features block creates an immersive, scroll-driven experience where each feature section dynamically changes the background as users navigate. Ideal for storytelling, product showcases, or highlighting core brand values.
The Map Main Store block displays your physical store location with an embedded map and address information. Ideal for brick-and-mortar businesses or brands with flagship locations.

The Multi Column block creates a responsive grid of content cards, each combining an image, heading, text, and button. Ideal for features, services, testimonials, or product highlights in a clean, structured layout.
The Newsletter block collects email subscriptions from visitors. It’s a key tool for building your marketing list and driving repeat traffic through email campaigns.

The Rich Text block provides a flexible container for combining a heading and rich-text content. It’s ideal for informational sections, policy summaries, storytelling, or any content that doesn’t require interactive elements like forms or product data.

The Scrolling Banner block displays a continuously moving text banner—ideal for announcements, promotions, shipping notices, or live updates. It creates dynamic visual interest without requiring user interaction.

The Slideshow block creates a full-featured carousel banner that supports images, videos, and 3D models as slide content. Ideal for hero banners, promotional campaigns, or immersive storytelling at the top of your homepage or landing pages.

The Store Messages block displays a row of informational or promotional messages—such as shipping notices, return policies, or trust badges—with optional icons and links. Ideal for headers, footers, or banners to reinforce key store policies.
The Testimonials block displays customer reviews or endorsements in a visually engaging carousel format. Ideal for building trust and social proof on homepages, product pages, or landing sections.

The Timelines block displays a chronological sequence of events, milestones, or process steps in a visually structured layout. Ideal for brand stories, product development journeys, service workflows, or company history.

The Video With Text block combines a video with descriptive content (heading, text, and button) in a flexible layout. Perfect for product demos, brand stories, or explainer content that benefits from both visual and textual context.
OfficeHub theme provides a set of universal block components that can be freely added to any section. These blocks ensure consistent design and flexible layout control across your store.
The Article Body Text block displays the full content of a blog post. It is only available in blog post templates.
The Blog Posts Lists block displays a grid or list of blog articles. It is only available in blog  templates (e.g., /blogs/news).

The List Collections Content block displays a grid of collections. It is used in Collections list templates or within composite blocks that require a collection listing. It supports one child block: Collection block.

The Page Body Text block displays the main content of a Shopify page (as authored in Shopify Admin > Pages). It is only available in page templates and has no configurable settings—it automatically renders the page’s rich text content, images, and embedded elements as defined in the Shopify admin.

The Product Description block displays the product’s full description as entered in Shopify Admin > Products. It is only available in product templates and must be added manually within other sections (e.g., a custom content section below the product media).
A block for displaying blog post cards—either as a single featured article or as part of a blog list/grid. Commonly used in blog index pages, sidebar highlights, or “Recommended Articles” sections.
The Cart Checkout block displays the checkout form inside the cart sidebar or cart page, including subtotal, order notes, policies, and action buttons.
The Column block is a single-column container used to divide a parent section into multiple columns. It supports all @theme child blocks.

The Filters block provides sidebar-based filtering functionality for collection pages and search results pages, allowing customers to refine products by variant options, price, availability, and more.

The Page Top Banner block appears at the top of inner pages (excluding the homepage) and is used to display a hero-style banner or breadcrumb navigation area. It supports dynamic background images and customizable overlay text for enhanced visual storytelling.
Product Cards are primarily used for product recommendation lists and collection pages.

The Default Page section is the main container for the main-page template, used for standard Shopify pages (e.g., About Us, Contact, FAQs). It provides a clean, flexible layout for rich content.

Editing the robots.txt file is an advanced and high-risk action. The default robots.txt provided by Shopify is already optimized for SEO, and in most cases, should not be modified. warning Even a small syntax error in robots.txt can block search engines from indexing your entire store, resulting in zero organic traffic. Our support team cannot be held responsible for issues caused by incorrect robots.txt customizations. Only proceed if you fully understand the implications.

Search engines like Google use automated programs called crawlers (or bots) to discover and index web pages. The robots.txt file acts as a set of instructions that tells these crawlers: Which pages or directories should be crawled Which pages should be ignored All Shopify stores come with a default, SEO-friendly robots.txt that: Allows crawling of product, collection, blog, and page URLs Blocks administrative and duplicate URLs (e.g., cart, search, sort parameters) Prevents indexing of low-value pages that could dilute SEO You can view your store’s current file at: https://your-store.com/robots.txt
Yes—but only if absolutely necessary (e.g., blocking staging pages, restricting API endpoints, or complying with legal requirements).

Shopify does not create a custom robots.txt by default—your store uses Shopify’s managed version. To override it, you must manually create a robots.txt.liquid file in your theme’s Assets folder. Once created, your version replaces Shopify’s default entirely—use with extreme caution. 📘 For step-by-step instructions, see Shopify’s official documentation on robots.txt.

Very rare scenarios include: Blocking specific URL patterns (e.g., /apps/, /search?q=*) Preventing indexing of a password-protected staging theme Complying with regional data regulations 🚫 Do NOT edit robots.txt to: “Improve SEO” (the default is already optimal) Hide low-quality content (fix the content instead) Block competitors (it doesn’t work that way)
documents.s: ✅ When Might You Need to Edit robots.txt?

documents.t: Leave it alone unless directed by an SEO specialist or legal requirement. If you’re unsure, do not create or modify robots.txt.liquid. 💡 Remember: A missing or invalid robots.txt is often safer than a misconfigured one. Search engines will simply crawl your site using standard rules.
Before reading this article, we strongly recommend reviewing Understanding Pagespeed Score to grasp core performance concepts. Performance optimization is an ongoing effort—not a one-time fix.

Potential improvement: Very High Apps are the #1 cause of performance degradation. A single poorly coded app can reduce your Pagespeed score by 10–20 points. ✅ Not all apps impact performance: Backend-only apps (e.g., inventory sync) often have no frontend effect. ❌ Frontend apps (e.g., pop-ups, reviews, loyalty) inject scripts that slow down your store. 🛑 Before installing: Ask: “Is this app essential to my business?” If not, skip it. 💬 Contact developers to understand their performance practices.

Potential improvement: Very High When you uninstall an app, it revokes the developer’s access—but doesn’t automatically remove its code from your theme. This “dead code” lingers and slows your store. ✅ Best practice: After uninstalling, contact the app developer to confirm if manual cleanup is needed. 🔍 Note: Modern apps using App Blocks (Online Store 2.0) auto-remove their code—no cleanup required.

Potential improvement: Very High Shopify optimizes images after upload, but pre-compression is critical. ✅ Before uploading: Use TinyPNG or Squoosh to compress JPG/PNG. Convert to WEBP (smaller than JPG/PNG with same quality). 🤖 Automate: Use apps like Crush.pics to auto-optimize new uploads.

Potential improvement: High ❌ Avoid GIF: Extremely heavy; use MP4 video for animations instead. ⚠️ Limit PNG: Only use when transparency is required (JPG doesn’t support it). PNG files are 2–3× larger than JPG. ✅ Prefer WEBP or JPG: Best balance of quality and file size.

Potential improvement: High We regularly release performance-optimized updates with: Bug fixes New features Faster code (e.g., lighter JavaScript, improved lazy loading) ✅ Action: Check for updates in Shopify Admin > Themes and upgrade if you’re on an older version.

Potential improvement: Medium Each section adds HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. More sections = slower load. ✅ Limit to 10–12 sections per page (see Best Practices for Using Sections). ❌ Avoid stacking multiple heavy sections (e.g., 3 carousels + video + 3D model).

Potential improvement: Medium Custom fonts require extra downloads, delaying text rendering. ✅ Use system fonts (e.g., System UI, San Francisco, Segoe UI)—they’re pre-installed on all devices. ❌ Avoid loading multiple Google Fonts or custom web fonts.

Potential improvement: Medium Videos enhance UX but impact performance—even with lazy loading. ✅ Max 4–6 videos per page. ✅ Use MP4 (hosted on Shopify) instead of YouTube/Vimeo (third-party scripts slow load times). 🎯 Place videos below the fold to avoid blocking LCP.

Potential improvement: Medium Never add analytics code directly to your theme. ✅ Use Shopify’s native integrations: Google Analytics → Shopify Admin > Settings > Analytics Meta Pixel → Shopify Admin > Marketing > Pixels ❌ Avoid pasting tracking scripts into theme.liquid—this blocks rendering.

Potential improvement: Medium Some Shopify features add heavy JavaScript: Dynamic checkout buttons (Apple Pay, PayPal, etc.) Shopify Inbox Wishlist apps ✅ Trade-off: Disabling these may improve performance but could reduce conversions. 🔬 Test first: Run A/B tests to measure impact on sales vs. speed.

Potential improvement: Small Some themes (e.g., Impact, Prestige) offer fade-in/fade-out page transitions. While visually smooth, they add ~150ms artificial delay per navigation. ✅ To disable: Open Theme Editor Go to Theme Settings > Animation Turn off “Show page transition” ⚠️ Note: OfficeHub does not include page transitions by default—this setting only applies if you’ve added it via custom code.

Focus on the top 3 fixes first: Audit and remove unused apps Compress and convert images to WEBP Limit sections to 12 per page These alone can boost your score by 20–30 points—with minimal effort. 🔗 Next step: Hire a vetted expert from the Shopify Partner Directory for advanced optimization (e.g., custom code cleanup, LCP tuning).

Performance is a complex yet critical topic—and a common source of confusion for merchants. This guide addresses shared concerns and provides actionable, realistic advice to improve your store’s performance—without chasing misleading scores.

Many tools exist (e.g., PageSpeed Insights, Lighthouse), but we recommend using Shopify’s built-in performance score (powered by Lighthouse and adapted for e-commerce). 📘 Learn more in Shopify’s official performance documentation.

Yes—but context matters. ✅ Good performance improves SEO and reduces bounce rates. ⚠️ But: A high Pagespeed score ≠ business success. E-commerce stores require rich media, apps, and dynamic features—unlike simple blogs. These inherently impact scores. 🎯 Key insight: If an app or feature boosts sales but lowers your score by 10–15 points, it’s often worth it. Prioritize user experience and conversion over perfect scores.

All OfficeHub themes are performance-optimized: Minimal, efficient JavaScript and CSS Smart image loading (e.g., LCP-aware lazy loading) Zero layout shifts (CLS-optimized by default) ✅ Trust us: We’ve spent hundreds of hours optimizing code. The theme is rarely the bottleneck. If your store is slow, the cause is almost always apps, media, or third-party scripts—not the theme.
documents.s: 🧩 How Does the Theme Impact Performance?

documents.t: It’s true that Dawn (Shopify’s free theme) may score slightly higher—but it’s not an apples-to-apples comparison: Feature Dawn (Free) OfficeHub (Premium) Sections ~10 basic sections 50+ advanced sections Media Basic image support Video, 3D models, galleries, carousels UX Minimal interactivity Rich interactions, quick-buy, sticky elements 💡 Trade-off: Advanced features = slightly lower scores. But if they increase conversions, the trade-off is justified.

Forget “100.” For real-world e-commerce stores, here’s a realistic benchmark: Score Range Interpretation 70+ Excellent. Faster than 99% of websites. No action needed. 45–70 Good. Functional for most users. Optimize only if you have bandwidth. 25–45 Acceptable, but may feel slow on mobile or 3G. Consider light cleanup. < 25 Poor. Likely hurting SEO and conversions. Take action. 📌 Goal: Aim for ≥50. Anything above 70 is exceptional for a feature-rich store.

Avoid “performance apps” or freelancers (e.g., on Fiverr) promising 90+ scores for $50. These often: Break core functionality (cart, checkout, analytics) Hide content from Google (via delayed rendering) Disable essential scripts (payment, tracking, personalization) 🛑 Result: Higher scores—but lower sales, broken tracking, and lost data. Not worth the risk.
Google’s Core Web Vitals directly impact your Pagespeed score. Here’s how OfficeHub handles them—and what you can do:

What it is: Unexpected layout shifts (e.g., images jumping after load). OfficeHub status: Optimized by default (no CLS from theme). Your action: Avoid apps that inject content after load Use width/height on images Prefer system fonts over custom web fonts (or use font-display: swap)

What it is: Time to load the main visual element (e.g., hero image, product photo). OfficeHub status: Smart preloading for likely LCP elements. Your action: Place slideshow or text hero as the first section on homepage Compress images (use WEBP, max 2560px wide) Avoid huge hero videos on slow connections

FID (First Input Delay) is being replaced by INP (Interaction to Next Paint) in 2024. Measures responsiveness to clicks, taps, and scrolls. OfficeHub status: Lightweight, deferred JavaScript. Your action: Remove unused apps (biggest cause of poor INP) Limit heavy sections (e.g., only 1 slideshow per page) Avoid “mega-menus” with 100+ links

Focus on high-impact, low-effort wins: Audit apps: Remove any unused or redundant apps. Optimize images: Convert to WEBP, compress, and use proper dimensions. Limit sections: Keep pages under 15 sections (see Best Practices for Using Sections). Avoid custom code: Unless absolutely necessary—every script adds weight. Test on real devices: Use Chrome DevTools > Lighthouse on mobile 3G throttling. 🔗 Next step: See our full guide: Improving Store Performance. 💡 Final Thought: Don’t optimize for robots—optimize for humans. A store that loads in 2.5 seconds with great UX will always outperform a “100-score” store that feels empty and lifeless.

Divider type: Symbol used between time units. Options: Colon – Standard : (e.g., 02:15:30:45) Dot – Small centered dot • Line – Vertical bar | None – No separator End date: Required. OfficeHub theme provides a set of universal block components that can be freely added to any section. These blocks ensure consistent design and flexible layout control across your store.

The following settings are available in nearly every main block and section, allowing you to customize layout, spacing, and appearance uniformly. Enable full width: Expands the block container to 100% of the viewport width (ignoring the site’s maximum content width). Ideal for full-bleed banners or backgrounds. Block class: Adds custom CSS classes to the block container—commonly used for utility classes like spacing (mt-4, pb-6) or custom styling hooks. Spacing utilities that apply to all breakpoints, from xs to xxl, have no breakpoint abbreviation in them. This is because those classes are applied from min-width: 0 and up, and thus are not bound by a media query. The remaining breakpoints, however, do include a breakpoint abbreviation. The classes are named using the format {property}{sides}-{size} for xs and {property}{sides}-{breakpoint}-{size} for sm, md, lg, xl, and xxl. Where property is one of: m - for classes that set margin p - for classes that set padding Where sides is one of: t - for classes that set margin-top or padding-top b - for classes that set margin-bottom or padding-bottom s - (start) for classes that set margin-left or padding-left in LTR, margin-right or padding-right in RTL e - (end) for classes that set margin-right or padding-right in LTR, margin-left or padding-left in RTL x - for classes that set both *-left and *-right y - for classes that set both *-top and *-bottom blank - for classes that set a margin or padding on all 4 sides of the element Where size is one of: 0 - for classes that eliminate the margin or padding by setting it to 0 1 - (by default) for classes that set the margin or padding to 0.25rem 2 - (by default) for classes that set the margin or padding to 0.5rem 3 - (by default) for classes that set the margin or padding to 1rem 4 - (by default) for classes that set the margin or padding to 1.5rem 5 - (by default) for classes that set the margin or padding to 2rem 6 - (by default) for classes that set the margin or padding to 2.5rem auto - for classes that set the margin to auto Examples: py-md-6 py-4 Background: Sets a solid color or gradient background for the block container. Or, use image: Instead of a solid background, apply a predefined background image style from your Theme Settings → Style scheme settings → Background Image Schema (configured in Theme Settings). This option leverages your pre-saved image, repeat, position, and attachment settings for consistency.

Scroll animations require the AOS (Animate On Scroll) library (aos.js) to be loaded. To enable this feature, go to Theme Settings → Advanced and turn on “Enabled animate element on scroll”. Once enabled, you can configure scroll animations on individual blocks using the following parameters: Animation: The type of entrance effect. Options include: fade, fade-up, fade-down, fade-left, fade-right, flip-up, flip-down, flip-left, flip-right, zoom-in, zoom-out, slide-up, slide-down, etc. Easing effects: Controls the acceleration curve of the animation. → Keep the default value unless you have a specific motion design requirement. Anchor Placement: Defines where in the viewport the animation should trigger. Options: top-bottom, top-center, top-top, center-bottom, etc. (e.g., top-bottom means the animation starts when the top of the element hits the bottom of the viewport) Duration: How long the animation lasts, in milliseconds (ms). Example: 600 = 0.6 seconds. Delay: Time to wait before starting the animation after it’s triggered, in milliseconds (ms). Example: 200 = 0.2-second delay.

The Article Body Text block displays the full content of a blog post. It is only available in blog post templates.

Show date: Display the article’s published date. Show author: Show the name of the article’s author. Show X (formerly Twitter) sharing icon: Enable the X/Twitter share button. Show Facebook sharing icon: Enable the Facebook share button. Show excerpt: Display the article’s excerpt (if defined in the Shopify admin). Show tags: Show the blog post’s assigned tags. Tags style: Styling for tags, using a preset from Theme Settings → Style scheme settings → Tags Style Schema.

Show prev/next link: Display navigation to the previous and next blog posts. Style: Visual style—button, outline, or link. Color schema: Text/button color from theme color variables. Size: Button size when style is button or outline—small, default, or large.

Show article directory tree: Generate a table of contents from headings (<h1> to <h6>) in the article. Width: Container width as a percentage (e.g., 25%, 30%). Position: Placement of the directory—left or right sidebar. Style schema: Card-style container for the directory, using a preset from Theme Settings → Style scheme settings → Cards Style Schema.

Style schema: Overall styling for the comments section, using a Theme Settings > Style scheme theme-settings > Cards Style Schema preset. Number per page: Maximum number of comments displayed per page. Paging: Pagination method—Infinite scroll or Show buttons. Infinite scroll: Automatically load the next page when scrolling Show buttons: Display pagination button Item color: Background or text color for individual comment blocks, selected from theme color variables. Show comment name: Display the commenter’s name. Show comment date: Show the date the comment was posted. Input style schema: Styling for the comment input field, from Theme Settings → Style scheme settings → Input Style Schema. Button style: Submit button appearance—button, outline. Button color schema: Button color from Theme Settings → Basic Settings → Colors. Button size: small, default, or large. Button alignment: Horizontal alignment of the submit button (left, center, right).
The Blog Posts Lists block displays a grid or list of blog articles. It is only available in blog templates (e.g., /blogs/news).

Blog block class: Custom CSS class applied to the blog posts container. Useful for spacing or layout overrides. Number per page: Maximum number of posts displayed per page. Per row on desktop: Number of posts per row on desktop (e.g., 2, 3, 4). Per row on mobile: Number of posts per row on mobile devices (typically 1 or 2). Enable masonry: Toggle masonry (variable-height) layout for uneven post heights. Paging: Pagination method—Infinite scroll or Show buttons. Infinite scroll: Automatically load the next page when scrolling Show buttons: Display pagination button

Show tag filter by: Display filter buttons for blog tags (e.g., “News”, “Tips”). Filter tags style: Styling for tag filter buttons, using a preset from Theme Settings → Style scheme settings → Tags Style Schema. Show view button: Show layout toggle (e.g., grid vs. list view)—if supported by theme. Show RSS feed link: Display an RSS icon linking to the blog’s feed (e.g., /blogs/news.atom). "Accessibility" encompasses a broad range of practices aimed at ensuring that people with disabilities—such as visual or motor impairments—can easily use your online store. This includes support for keyboard navigation, screen readers, and other assistive technologies. At Scenario, we take accessibility seriously. Our themes are built using industry best practices, and we are committed to continuous improvement to ensure your store is usable by everyone.

The Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) is a civil rights law that prohibits discrimination based on disability (Wikipedia). In the digital context, the ADA implies that website owners should follow certain accessibility guidelines—such as providing keyboard navigation, alternative text for images and icons, and semantic HTML structure. Achieving full ADA compliance can be a complex and ongoing process. We cannot guarantee 100% ADA compliance at this time. However, our themes implement numerous accessibility best practices to support an inclusive user experience. To date, we have not received any reports of ADA-related lawsuits stemming from the use of our themes. ⚠️ Important: If you ever receive an ADA-related legal claim specifically tied to issues caused by our theme (which is extremely rare), please contact our support team immediately. We will assist in resolving theme-related accessibility concerns.
While our theme provides a strong accessibility foundation, you—as the store owner—also share responsibility for maintaining an accessible experience. Here’s how you can help:

Although our theme is optimized for accessibility, third-party apps may introduce non-compliant code. ✅ Recommendation: Contact the developers of any apps you use to inquire about their accessibility policies and compliance status.

Users with visual impairments often rely on screen readers. Vague or generic text can be confusing. ❌ Avoid: “Learn more” ✅ Prefer: “Learn more about our summer dresses” Clear, contextual labels improve understanding for all users, especially those using assistive technologies.

Our theme offers extensive color customization, but you are responsible for choosing accessible color combinations. Aim for at least WCAG AA-level contrast between text and background. Use free tools like WebAIM Contrast Checker to validate your choices.

While videos can be engaging, they are not always accessible. Always provide text alternatives (e.g., transcripts or descriptive captions). Prefer images with descriptive alt text and clear written content as your primary means of communication. Use video as a supplemental—not sole—method of conveying key information. By following these practices alongside our accessible theme foundation, you can create a more inclusive and legally resilient storefront. For further guidance, consider consulting an accessibility specialist or conducting an accessibility audit of your live store.

According to Shopify’s Terms of Service, Section 9.4, you must have a valid license to use our theme in your store. The only way to obtain a valid license is by purchasing the theme directly from the official Shopify Theme Store.

A single theme license is valid for one Shopify store only. For example, if you purchased the theme for my-first-store.myshopify.com, it may only be used on that store. You may only use the theme on a different store after officially transferring the license—a process governed by Shopify. Important OfficeHub does not offer refunds, discounts, or bulk theme purchases. All theme sales and licensing are managed exclusively by Shopify.

If you purchased the theme from the Shopify Theme Store, you likely have a valid license. To confirm: Contact Shopify Support and ask them to verify your license, or Reach out to our support team with your store URL.

If you obtained the theme from any source other than the Shopify Theme Store, your store is likely using an unauthorized (unlicensed) copy. Consequences include: ❌ No access to support or theme updates ⚠️ Risk of legal action: We reserve the right to report your store to Shopify’s legal team and file a DMCA takedown notice, which could result in your store being suspended. ✅ To avoid disruption, please either: Purchase the theme from the Shopify Theme Store, or Completely remove our theme from your store.
documents.s: What If My Store Doesn’t Have a Valid License?

documents.t: You may only import the theme into another store if that store has its own valid license purchased from the Shopify Theme Store. Simply copying or transferring theme files between stores without a license violates Shopify’s Terms of Service.
documents.s: Can I Import the Theme from Another Store?

documents.t: ✅ Same Shopify store, multiple markets (e.g., US and EU storefronts under one admin): → Only one license is required. ❌ Separate Shopify stores for each market: → You must purchase one license per store.
documents.s: What If I Operate Multiple Markets?

documents.t: If you’re an agency building stores for clients, you may use a password-protected development store to test and customize the theme—at no extra cost—provided that: The development store does not accept real payments The store is not publicly accessible (i.e., password-protected)

The theme must be purchased on the live (production) store, not the development store. When contacting our support team about a development store, always include the URL of the licensed (live) store in your message. This helps us verify your license quickly.

License transfers are handled exclusively by Shopify. To transfer a theme license from one store to another: Contact Shopify Support directly for instructions. Be aware that Shopify typically requires the original store to be fully closed before a license can be transferred. ❗ As of now, Shopify does not allow license transfers while keeping the original store active. If you still need to operate the original store, a transfer is not possible—and you’ll need to purchase a new license for the second store. For any licensing questions, please contact Shopify Support or our support team with your licensed store URL.

Heading (optional top banner in Mega menu) Heading: Title text Tag: HTML tag (<h1>–<h6> or <div>) Size: Font size from typography variables Color schema: Text color from theme variables Alignment: Text alignment Text (optional description below heading) Text: Rich text content Size, Color schema, Alignment: Same as above Sub navigation Style: Layout type—tabs-horizontal, tabs-vertical, or grid Tabs style: nav-tabs (standard) or nav-pills (capsule) Number per row: Columns in grid layout Featured images Enable featured medias: Show media (image/video) in Mega menu Width: Media width as percentage Order: Position—left or right Supported Child Blocks​ All child blocks share common settings: Heading: Tab or grid title Tag: HTML tag for heading Url: Link destination Specific block types: Mega products​ Displays product cards. Select a card styling preset from your Cards Style Schema (defined in Theme Settings → Style Schemes → Cards Style Schema). Image: Configure the image using the same settings as the Blocks → Basic Block → Image (e.g., cropping, ratio, mobile override, link). Heading: Customize the title using the same parameters as the Blocks → Basic Block → Heading (e.g., tag, size, color, alignment, icon). Text: Add and style rich text content using the same options as the Blocks → Basic Block → Text. Button: Add a call-to-action button with settings matching the Blocks → Basic Block → Button (e.g., label, URL, style, color, size).
A static block that appears below the mobile off-canvas menu. Configuration follows Blocks → Composite Function Block → Featured Products. Can be hidden if not needed.

The Modal Top Bar is a modal section that appears at the top of the page when the search icon is clicked. It provides an expanded search interface with predictive results and optional hot links. This section is functionally tied to the Top Bar block and shares its core settings. ⚠️ Note: For the search modal to work, this section must be present in your theme. If missing, the search icon will not trigger the search bar.
Predictive search is enabled by default. You can disable or configure it in Shopify admin → Theme Settings → Search Style Schema.
Search bar styling is controlled by a preset from: Theme Settings → Style scheme settings → Search Bar Style Schema.

Title: Heading for the hot links section (e.g., “Quick Links”). Title style: Styling for the title, using a preset from: Theme Settings → Style scheme settings → Tags Style Schema. Hot links: Select a Shopify menu (from Navigation) to populate the link list. Links style: Visual style for the links, using the same Tags Style Schema. Links alignment: Horizontal alignment of the hot links (left, center, right).
Enable entrance animations as block enter the viewport. Configuration follows the standard Animations on Scroll settings. See: Blocks → Overview → Animations on scroll

The Cart Sidebar section displays a slide-in cart panel on all pages except the dedicated cart page. To enable it, go to Shopify Admin → Themes → Customize → Theme Settings → Cart and set Cart type = Sidebar.
Background: Solid or gradient background color for the sidebar. Text color: Global text color, selected from Theme Settings → Basic Settings → Colors.

Show cart items number: Display item count badge when cart contains ≥1 item. Color: Badge text color from Theme Settings → Basic Settings → Colors. Size: Font size using typography variables from Theme Settings → Basic Settings → Typography.

Displays cart items and optional free shipping progress bar (configured in Theme Settings → Cart → Free shipping bar). Show backorder text: Shows availability notice for out-of-stock items that can still be purchased.

Size: Small / Default / Large Background: Selector background color from Theme Settings → Basic Settings → Colors. Text/border color schema: Text and border color from Theme Settings → Basic Settings → Colors.

Show inventory notice: Toggle low-stock alerts. Show count in inventory notice: Never Do not display the inventory count. When inventory low Show the count only when stock falls below the defined low-inventory threshold. Always Display the inventory count at all times, regardless of stock level. Show announcement alert: Display custom promotional or informational banner. Position: Above cart items Display the inventory count at all times, regardless of stock level. Below cart items Show the alert immediately after the list of cart items, but before the subtotal and checkout area. Above subtotal Place the alert just above the subtotal line (and any associated shipping or tax summaries). Below checkout button Position the alert at the very bottom of the cart sidebar, underneath the primary checkout button. Text: Alert message content. Icon: Optional prefix icon. Icon size: Icon scale as percentage. Background, Text color: From Theme Settings → Basic Settings → Colors. Text size: Font size from Theme Settings → Basic Settings → Typography.
Icon: Graphic shown when cart is empty. Icon size: Icon scale as percentage.

Displays product recommendations configured in the Featured Products block. Position: Cart item below: Below items (when cart not empty) Empty cart below: Below empty state content Both: Show in both contexts Hide: Disable entirely
Section title (e.g., “Your Cart”). Settings follow Blocks → Basic Block → Heading.
Title for empty state (e.g., “Your cart is empty”). Settings follow Blocks → Basic Block → Heading.
Supporting message (e.g., “Start shopping to fill it up!”). Settings follow Blocks → Basic Block → Text.
Call-to-action (e.g., “Continue Shopping”). Settings follow Blocks → Basic Block → Button.
Full checkout controls (subtotal, notes, buttons). Settings follow Blocks → Subblocks of Specific Block → Cart Checkout.

The Pop Up section creates a modal dialog that appears automatically when a page loads. It’s ideal for capturing leads, promoting offers, announcing launches, or displaying important messages (e.g., age verification, shipping delays, or newsletter sign-ups).

Section class: Custom CSS class for spacing or layout overrides. Background: Set a solid or gradient background color. Or, use image: Apply a background image using a preset from Theme Settings → Style scheme settings → Background Image Schema. Size: Modal width—small, default, large, or extra large. Overlay opacity: Transparency of the dark backdrop behind the modal (0–100%).
You can include any combination of the following inside the pop-up modal:
Modal title (e.g., “Get 10% Off Your First Order”). Settings follow Blocks → Basic Block → Heading.
Supporting message or terms. Settings follow Blocks → Basic Block → Text.
Primary action (e.g., “Close” or “Submit”). Settings follow Blocks → Basic Block → Button.
Email subscription input with Shopify integration. Settings follow Blocks → Basic Block → Newsletter form.
Full contact form for inquiries (see Blocks → Basic Block → Contact Form).
Urgency-driven timer for flash sales. Settings follow Blocks → Basic Block → Countdown timer.
Embedded or self-hosted video content. Settings follow Blocks → Basic Block → Video.
Static promotional or product image. Settings follow Blocks → Basic Block → Image.

Interactive product visualization. Settings follow Blocks → Basic Block → 3D model. 🌟 Tip: Use pop-ups sparingly and always include a clear close button to avoid frustrating users. For best results, trigger them after a short delay or on exit intent.

In the OfficeHub theme, every Section is a flexible container built from Blocks. You can freely add, reorder, and configure blocks within any section to create unique layouts—no coding required. All sections are designed to be modular, responsive, and performance-optimized, giving you full creative control while maintaining speed and usability. Below is the complete list of available sections. Click any link to view detailed settings and configuration options.

Featured Collection Showcase products from a collection in a responsive grid or carousel. Featured Product Display a single product with full media gallery, variant picker, and buy options. Rich Text Add custom headings, paragraphs, lists, and styled content. Image With Text Combine images and text in flexible layouts (side-by-side, overlay, stacked). Slideshow Create full-width or contained carousels with images, video, or 3D models. Newsletter Embed a mailing list signup form with customizable styling. Custom Liquid Insert raw Liquid, HTML, or JavaScript for advanced customizations. 3D Model With Text Display interactive 3D models alongside descriptive content. Background Video Use a video as a full-width background with overlay text. Blog Posts Feature recent articles from any blog in a card-based grid. Carousel Build custom slideshows with mixed content (image, video, 3D, text). Contact Us Combine heading, text, and a contact form in one section. Countdown Timer Add urgency with a live countdown to sales, launches, or events. Faq Display collapsible frequently asked questions with optional search. General Section A blank canvas for full creative freedom—add any combination of blocks. Hotspots Add interactive clickable points over an image (e.g., product details). Key Features Highlight benefits or services with icons, headings, and short descriptions. Map Dealer Multi Store Show multiple store locations on an interactive map. Map Main Store Display a single flagship store location with contact info. Multi Columns Create responsive multi-column layouts (2–4 columns) with rich content. Product Description Render the full product description (from Shopify admin) in any layout. Scrolling Banner Display a continuously scrolling announcement bar (e.g., “Free shipping!”). Scrollspy Section Create tabbed navigation that highlights as users scroll through content. Sidebar Section Build pages with a main content area and a customizable sidebar. Tabs Section Organize content into switchable tabs (e.g., Specs, Shipping, Reviews). Testimonials Display customer reviews or quotes in a carousel or grid. Timelines Visualize processes, milestones, or brand history in a vertical timeline. Video With Text Pair embedded or uploaded videos with descriptive text and calls-to-action.

The 3D Model With Text section is designed to showcase products using an interactive 3D model alongside descriptive content such as a heading, rich text, and call-to-action button. It supports advanced features like automatic rotation and autoplay for embedded media. This section is ideal for highlighting product details in an immersive, engaging way—especially for complex or premium items where 3D visualization adds significant value. For full configuration options—including layout, overlay settings, child blocks, and 3D model controls—see: Blocks → Composite Function Block → 3D Model With Text

The Background Video section displays a full-width or full-viewport video as a dynamic background, with optional overlaid text content (heading, description, and call-to-action button). It’s ideal for hero sections, brand storytelling, or immersive landing pages. This section leverages the same robust configuration as the Video With Text block, including layout options, overlay styling, and video controls. For complete setup instructions—including video settings, layout, overlay opacity, play button options, and child block configuration—see: Blocks → Composite Function Block → Video With Text

The Blog Posts section displays a grid of articles from a selected blog anywhere on your store—ideal for homepages, landing pages, or dedicated content hubs. It supports responsive layouts, masonry grids, and rich card styling. For full configuration details—including blog selection, layout options, card styling, and child block settings—see: Blocks → Composite Function Block → Blog Posts

The Carousel section implements a responsive, Bootstrap-based slideshow that supports images, videos, and 3D models as slide content. Use it anywhere on your store to create engaging visual narratives, product showcases, or promotional banners. For full configuration details—including autoplay, navigation controls, pagination styles, and child block settings—see: Blocks → Composite Function Block → Carousel

The Contact Us section provides a ready-to-use layout for displaying a contact form alongside a heading and descriptive text. It can be added to any page—such as a dedicated contact page, footer, or sidebar—to help customers reach out with inquiries, support requests, or feedback. For full configuration details—including form fields, styling, button settings, and child block options—see: Blocks → Composite Function Block → Contact Us

The Countdown Timer section displays a dynamic countdown to a specific date and time—perfect for creating urgency around flash sales, product launches, or limited-time offers. It includes a fully configurable countdown block with customizable labels, styling, and layout options. For complete setup instructions—including target date, time zone, label text, typography, color scheme, and layout—see: Blocks → Composite Function Block → Countdown Timer

The Custom Liquid section allows you to embed raw Liquid, HTML, CSS, or JavaScript code directly into any page of your store. This is ideal for advanced customizations, third-party integrations, dynamic content rendering, or implementing logic that isn’t supported by standard blocks. For full configuration details—including background settings, container width, and Liquid code input—see: Blocks → Composite Function Block → Custom Liquid Block

The Faq section displays a set of frequently asked questions with collapsible answers and an integrated keyword search bar—ideal for reducing support inquiries and improving user self-service. It supports an optional index sidebar for quick navigation in long FAQ lists. For full configuration details—including index column, search functionality, styling, and child block settings—see: Blocks → Composite Function Block → Faq Collapsible Tabs

The Featured Collection section highlights products from a selected collection or custom product list using a Swiper-powered carousel with advanced transition effects. It’s perfect for showcasing bestsellers, new arrivals, seasonal items, or promotional bundles in a visually dynamic way. For full configuration details—including product source, carousel effects, autoplay, pagination styling, and responsive layout settings—see: Blocks → Composite Function Block → Featured Collection

The Featured Product section displays a single product with the same rich, interactive experience as a full product detail page—including media gallery, variant picker, price, description, and buy buttons. Use it to highlight hero items, bestsellers, or new arrivals anywhere on your store (e.g., homepage, landing pages, or collections). For full configuration details—including gallery layout, variant controls, buy button styling, collapsible tabs, complementary products, and quick-buy integration—see: Blocks → Composite Function Block → Featured Product

The General Section is a fully flexible container that supports any block available in the OfficeHub theme. It’s ideal for building custom layouts, combining content types, or prototyping unique page sections without structural constraints.

To create multi-column designs within this section: Add the Columns Layout block. Inside it, add one or more Column blocks. Within each Column, insert any combination of blocks (e.g., images, text, product cards, forms). For full configuration details—including column width, sticky behavior, and responsive alignment—see: Blocks → Composite Function Block → Columns Layout

The Hotspots section displays an interactive image with multiple clickable or hoverable points that reveal contextual content—such as product details, descriptions, or calls to action. It’s ideal for lifestyle scenes, room layouts, product bundles, or any visual where users benefit from exploring specific areas. For full configuration details—including desktop/mobile positioning, hotspot styling, content card behavior, and child block support—see: Blocks → Composite Function Block → Hotspots

The Image With Text section combines a visual image with descriptive content—including a heading, rich text, and optional call-to-action button. It supports flexible layouts such as text on the left/right or overlaid directly on the image with customizable opacity, making it ideal for feature highlights, promotional banners, or storytelling. For full configuration details—including layout options, overlay settings, image styling, and child block controls—see: Blocks → Composite Function Block → Image With Text

The Key Features section creates an immersive, scroll-driven experience where each feature panel dynamically changes the background—ideal for storytelling, product journeys, or highlighting core brand values across full-screen segments. For full configuration details—including background colors, gradients, child block support (image, video, 3D model, heading, text), and scroll-based transitions—see: Blocks → Composite Function Block → Key Features

The Map Dealer Multi Store section displays multiple store or dealer locations on an interactive map, enabling customers to find nearby points of sale by keyword search, address, or region. Ideal for brands with physical retail partners, franchise networks, or multiple warehouse locations.

This section combines two key components: Store listing and search interface – built using the Map Main Store block structure (for layout, columns, and styling). Interactive multi-location map – powered by the Dealer Multi Store Map block (for map rendering, location pins, and search functionality). For full setup instructions: Layout, alignment, and column settings: see Blocks → Composite Function Block → Map Main Store Map-specific features (location pins, geocoding, search, clustering): see Blocks → Basic Block → Dealer Multi Store Map

The Map Main Store section displays your primary physical store location using an embedded Google Map, paired with your address, contact information, and optional call-to-action button. It’s ideal for brick-and-mortar businesses, flagship stores, or brands that want to emphasize local presence. For full configuration details—including layout alignment, column widths, sticky behavior, and child block settings (heading, text, button, and store map)—see: Blocks → Composite Function Block → Map Main Store

The Multi Columns section displays content in a responsive grid of cards—each combining an image, heading, text, and button. It’s ideal for showcasing features, services, product categories, testimonials, or any content that benefits from a clean, structured, multi-item layout. For full configuration details—including column count (desktop/mobile), card styling, image cropping, and child block settings—see: Blocks → Composite Function Block → Multi Column

The Newsletter section collects visitor email addresses to grow your marketing list and enable ongoing customer engagement through email campaigns. It includes a heading, descriptive text, and a fully functional subscription form that integrates with your store’s email marketing provider. For full configuration details—including layout width, background styling, and child block settings (heading, text, form)—see: Blocks → Composite Function Block → Newsletter

The Product Description section displays the full product description as authored in Shopify Admin > Products. It is designed exclusively for use in product templates and allows you to insert the description directly as a standalone section—ideal for placing detailed content below media, above reviews, or within custom layouts. This section has no configurable settings—it automatically renders the product’s rich-text description, including paragraphs, lists, images, and embedded media, exactly as entered in the Shopify admin.

The Rich Text section provides a clean, flexible container for displaying large blocks of formatted content—such as brand stories, policy details, editorial content, or instructional text. It supports a heading and a rich-text area with full formatting options (paragraphs, lists, links, bold/italic, etc.). For full configuration details—including background styling, container width, and child block settings (heading and text)—see: Blocks → Composite Function Block → Rich Text

The Scrolling Banner section displays a continuously moving text banner—ideal for announcements, promotions, shipping notices, or live updates. It creates dynamic visual interest without requiring user interaction and is commonly used in headers, footers, or as a standalone promotional strip. For full configuration details—including scroll direction (left, right, up, down), speed (interval), height settings, and child block options (heading and button)—see: Blocks → Composite Function Block → Scrolling Banner

The Scrollspy Section creates an interactive tabbed interface where: Clicking a tab scrolls the page to its corresponding content area. As the user scrolls, the active tab is automatically highlighted based on the visible section. This is ideal for long-form pages (e.g., product details, FAQs, or landing pages) that benefit from in-page navigation.
Each Tab / Scrollspy Pane represents a single tab and its associated content container.

Name: The label displayed in the tab navigation (e.g., “Specifications”, “Reviews”). Block class: Custom CSS class for the section (useful for spacing or styling). Active show: Manually set this pane as the initially active/highlighted tab on page load.
Supports all @theme blocks (e.g., Heading, Text, Product Cards, Image, etc.). Also supports @app blocks (app embeds and app blocks), enabling dynamic third-party content within tabs.

The Sidebar Section creates a layout with a main content area and a dedicated sidebar—ideal for blog posts, documentation pages, or product detail pages where you want to display supplementary content (e.g., “About Us,” contact forms, or related links) in a fixed or flexible sidebar. This section supports all @theme blocks in the main area and includes one required child block: Sidebar block.
Background: Sidebar background color, selected from Theme Settings → Basic Settings → Colors. Shadow: Drop shadow for depth—options: None, Default, Small, Large.

Sidebar Title​ Adds a heading to the top of the sidebar. Settings follow Blocks → Basic Block → Heading. Sidebar Text​ Inserts custom rich-text content (e.g., descriptions, calls to action). Settings follow Blocks → Basic Block → Text. Contact Form​ Embeds a functional contact form directly in the sidebar. Full configuration: Blocks → Composite Function Block → Contact Form. Sidebar Article​ Displays a list of recent blog posts. Blog: Select a blog to pull articles from. Limit: Maximum number of posts to show. Icon: Optional icon before each link (or no icon). Show article image: Toggle post thumbnails. Text truncate: Automatically shorten long titles. Hidden on mobile: Hide this block on mobile devices. Sidebar Blog Tags​ Shows tags from a specific blog or the current article. Blog: If not set: On blog post pages, displays tags from the current article only. If set: Shows all tags from the selected blog (visible on all pages). Limit: Max number of tags to display. Style: Tag styling from Theme Settings → Style scheme settings → Tags Style Schema. Hidden on mobile: Hide on mobile. Sidebar Links​ Renders a menu as a sidebar link list. Menu links: Select a Shopify menu (from Navigation in admin). Limit: Max number of links to show. Icon: Optional prefix icon (or no icon). Text truncate: Shorten long link text. Hidden on mobile: Hide on mobile. Sidebar Product​ Lists featured or related products. From collection: Pull products from a specific collection. Or, products list: Manually select products (takes precedence over collection). Limit: Max number of products. Icon: Optional icon before product name. Show product image: Display product thumbnails. Text truncate: Shorten long product titles. Hidden on mobile: Hide on mobile. Sidebar Collection​ Displays a list of collections. Collections list: Manually select collections to feature. Icon: Optional prefix icon (or no icon). Show collection image: Show collection thumbnails. Text truncate: Shorten long collection names. Hidden on mobile: Hide on mobile.

The Slideshow section creates a full-featured, responsive carousel banner that supports images, videos, and 3D models as slide content. It’s ideal for hero sections, promotional campaigns, or immersive storytelling at the top of your homepage or landing pages. For full configuration details—including slide effects, autoplay, navigation controls, pagination styling, overlay settings, and child block options (heading, text, button)—see: Blocks → Composite Function Block → Slideshow

The Tabs Section creates a tabbed interface that allows users to switch between different content panes within the same area. Unlike the Scrollspy Section (which scrolls the page), this section hides inactive panes and only displays the content of the currently selected tab—ideal for organizing dense information like specifications, reviews, or care instructions. 💡 Key difference from Scrollspy Section: Tabs Section: Clicking a tab instantly shows/hides content (no page scroll). Scrollspy Section: Clicking a tab scrolls to an anchored section; content remains on-page.
Each Tab / Scrollspy Pane represents a single tab and its associated content container.

Name: The label displayed in the tab navigation (e.g., “Specifications”, “Reviews”). Block class: Custom CSS class for the section (useful for spacing or styling). Active show: Manually set this pane as the initially active/highlighted tab on page load.
Supports all @theme blocks (e.g., Heading, Text, Product Cards, Image, etc.). Also supports @app blocks (app embeds and app blocks), enabling dynamic third-party content within tabs.

The Testimonials section displays customer reviews, endorsements, or user-generated content in a visually engaging carousel format. It’s a powerful tool for building trust, showcasing social proof, and reinforcing credibility across your store—especially on homepages, product pages, or landing sections. For full configuration details—including autoplay settings, testimonial card styling, media support (image/video/3D model), rating stars, and child block options (heading, text, video, image)—see: Blocks → Composite Function Block → Testimonials

The Timelines section presents content in a chronological, story-driven format—perfect for showcasing brand history, product development milestones, service workflows, or project roadmaps. Each timeline entry can include media (image, video, or 3D model), descriptive text, and custom icons, creating an engaging narrative experience. For full configuration details—including icon selection, card styling, time label formatting, responsive column layout, and child block support—see: Blocks → Composite Function Block → Timelines

The Video With Text section combines a video with descriptive content—including a heading, rich text, and call-to-action button—in a flexible layout. It supports multiple arrangements: text overlaid on the video, or text positioned to the left or right. Ideal for product demos, brand stories, explainer content, or full-viewport background video experiences. For full configuration details—including layout options, overlay opacity, play button settings, video width, and child block controls—see: Blocks → Composite Function Block → Video With Text

The Article Sidebar template enables you to create blog post pages with a dedicated sidebar—ideal for displaying related content such as author info, popular articles, tags, newsletter signups, or social sharing alongside your article.

Start from the Default Blog Post template Use the standard blog post layout as your base. Hide the default Article Body Text block In the main section, locate and hide or remove the Article body text block to prevent duplicate content rendering. Add a Sidebar Section Insert the Sidebar Section into your page layout. Configure the Sidebar Inside the Sidebar Section, use the Sidebar block to add dynamic content such as: Blog tags (auto-populated from the current article) Recent or related articles Author bio, social links, or sharing buttons Newsletter form or featured products Full settings: Sidebar Section Re-add Article Body Text inside the Sidebar Section To ensure your article content appears next to the sidebar (not below it), drag the Article Body Text block into the main content area of the Sidebar Section (not inside the sidebar column itself). The Default Blog Post section is the main container for the main-article template, used on individual blog post pages (e.g., /blogs/news/my-post). It provides a structured layout for article content, metadata, sharing, and related features.
Full width: Expand the article page to 100% of the viewport width. Main section class: Custom CSS class for the entire article section (useful for spacing or custom styling).

Position: Placement relative to page content (e.g., below title or above article body). Link color schema: Text color for breadcrumb links, selected from Theme Settings → Basic Settings → Colors. Alignment: Horizontal alignment—left, center, or right.
Controls the inner-page hero area (title, background image, overlay). Full settings: Blocks → Subblocks of Specific Block → Page Top Banner.
Renders the full blog post content, including date, author, tags, sharing buttons, comments, and table of contents. Full configuration: Blocks → Specific Page Block → Article Body Text.
The Blog Sidebar template allows you to create blog index pages with a dedicated sidebar—perfect for featuring popular posts, tags, newsletter signups, or related content alongside your article list.

Start from the Default Blog template Use the standard blog layout as your foundation. Hide the default Blog Posts Lists block In the main section, locate and hide or remove the Blog posts lists block to avoid duplication. Add a Sidebar Section Insert the Sidebar Section into your page layout. Enhance with Additional Blocks The Sidebar Section fully supports all @theme blocks in both the main content area and the sidebar column, giving you complete flexibility to build a rich, engaging blog layout. 💡 Tip: Use the “Hidden on mobile” option in sidebar child blocks to optimize space on small screens, or enable “Collapse” mobile layout for an accordion-style experience.

The Default Blog section is the main container for the main-blog template, used on blog index pages (e.g., /blogs/news). It displays a list of published articles with optional filtering, sharing, and layout controls.
Full width: Expand the blog page to 100% of the viewport width. Main section class: Custom CSS class for the entire blog section (useful for spacing or custom styling).

Controls the inner-page hero area (title, background image, overlay). Full settings: Blocks → Subblocks of Specific Block → Page Top Banner.
Renders the grid or list of blog articles with full customization options. For setting up blog posts cards, please refer to: Blocks → Specific Page Block → Blog Posts Lists

documents.t: Our theme includes a wide variety of unique sections to help you build rich, polished pages. But as the saying goes: “With great power comes great responsibility.” This guide outlines best practices to help you use our theme effectively—without compromising performance, usability, or maintainability. 💡 Note: As stated in Shopify’s Terms of Service, Section 9.4, themes purchased from the Shopify Theme Store are licensed for one store at a time. You may modify the theme, but you remain responsible for your store’s content and performance.
It’s tempting to add many sections to a single page, but we strongly recommend limiting each page to 10–15 sections. Here’s why:
Every section adds to the page’s rendering time. Fewer sections = faster load times = better user experience and higher conversion rates.
Too many sections can overwhelm visitors. A cleaner layout helps customers focus on your products and key messages.
Fewer sections mean less content to manage, update, and test—freeing you to focus on what truly matters.

Instead of cramming everything onto your homepage (e.g., a brand story, testimonials, and product highlights), split content into dedicated pages: Create an “About Us” page for your brand story Use a “Collections” page for product categories Build a “Reviews” page for social proof This approach distributes content across multiple URLs, improving your site’s structure and boosting organic search visibility.
Limits may feel restrictive, but they exist for good reason—based on over 10 years of e-commerce experience and real-world user behavior data.

Shopify enforces a hard limit of 25 unique sections per theme. This is a platform-level restriction designed to protect performance. ➡️ If you hit this limit, rethink your store structure instead of trying to bypass it. Often, consolidating or repurposing sections yields better results.

Shopify supports up to 3 levels of nested menu items. This cannot be increased—it’s based on usability best practices. ➡️ If your menu feels too deep, simplify your information architecture (e.g., group related items under clearer headings).

It’s natural to want to customize beyond the theme’s defaults—but avoid making changes based on assumptions. ✅ Do this instead: Use Shopify Analytics, Google Analytics, or heatmaps (e.g., Hotjar) to identify real user pain points. Gather customer feedback through surveys or usability testing. Only customize or override theme behavior when data shows a clear need. If you do identify a genuine issue that requires code-level changes, consider hiring a Shopify Expert.

Our theme is designed to solve ~90% of common e-commerce needs out of the box. But it’s not a one-size-fits-all solution—and it’s not meant to replace a fully custom-designed store built specifically for your brand. Trying to accommodate every possible use case would result in: Overly complex settings Confusing UI for merchants Poor performance and bloated code

Work with the theme—not against it. Embrace the decisions we’ve made based on industry best practices. You’ll save time, reduce technical debt, and often achieve better results than forcing a custom workaround.

Our themes come pre-translated into more than 12 languages, with carefully crafted default wording for buttons, labels, and interface elements (e.g., “Add to cart,” “Search,” “Sold out”). However, you may want to customize these phrases to better reflect your brand’s voice, tone, or style.

In your Shopify admin, go to Online Store > Themes. Find the theme you want to edit and click the three-dot “More actions” button. Select “Edit default theme content” from the dropdown menu. You’ll see a list of all pre-defined text strings used in the theme, organized by language. To quickly find a specific phrase, type the first few letters into the “Filter” box at the top. Click on any field and replace the default text with your custom wording. Example: Default: Add to cart Custom: Add to bag or I want this! Changes are saved automatically—no need to click “Save.” 🌐 Multilingual stores: If your store supports multiple languages, repeat this process for each language version to ensure consistency.
documents.s: ✏️ How to Edit Default Theme Content

documents.t: Keep it clear and concise: Custom wording should still be instantly understandable to customers. Avoid over-branding: Phrases like “Add to mystical treasure chest” may confuse users—prioritize usability. Test on mobile: Ensure your custom text fits well on all screen sizes. Don’t remove essential context: For example, changing “Unavailable” to just “—” may mislead shoppers.

While you could edit text directly in the theme’s .json or .liquid files, using “Edit default theme content” is: Safer (no risk of breaking code) Easier to maintain (changes persist through theme updates) Fully reversible 🔧 If you need dynamic or conditional text (e.g., personalized messages), that requires code customization. In such cases, consider hiring a Shopify Expert. 💡 Pro Tip: Use this feature to align microcopy with seasonal campaigns, product launches, or brand refreshes—without touching a single line of code!
